correctness.rationale: Projection onto a signed coordinate simplex yields the explicit positive barycentric inequalities. Taking worst signs and maximal face size reduces all faces exactly to ||b||_1+(d-2)||b||_infinity<1. A finite halfspace description and rank of active normals prove all 3^d-1 vertices and d*2^d facets, and 2^d*d! coordinate chambers of determinant one yield the binomial volume. The actual saved checker was executed with exact fractions on d=3..6, 1076 vertices, 324016 halfspace evaluations and 640 all-face projection tests; the proof covers all d>=4.

originality.rationale: Pavlík defines the kernel but supplies no higher-dimensional regular-cross-polytope exact shape or binomial volume. The previously published 3D full-normal-locus case is explicitly excluded. Canonical signohedron literature gives coefficient one in any dimension, the same only when d=3; the new all-face geometry forces coefficient d-2 for d>=4. Actual published-finding corpus/own-ledger/primary web comparisons did not show an implication-equivalent broader claim; historical priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: Full text of the two canonical-signohedron published records and the full-normal-locus published record was unavailable; statements beyond the accessible indexed summaries cannot be excluded.
An earlier arbitrary-parameter mixed-norm volume theorem could subsume the volume calculation, though it would still need an all-face kernel identification.
Alternative names (orthic kernel, full-normal locus, normal-admissibility region) may conceal prior higher-dimensional geometric statements.

value.rationale: A motivated and newly formalized all-face perpendicular-foot region is completely classified for a natural high-dimensional nonsimplicial family. The exact binomial probability describes exponentially rare admissibility for uniformly sampled centers, linked to a precise 3^d−1-vertex closed-polytope census. This is structural geometric content beyond the already known octahedral case and canonical coefficient-one norm ball; there is no assertion of higher-dimensional tiling results.
